title: Caesar Cipher
hints: Normalise the shift into `0..<26` first (Swift's `%` keeps the sign), then shift each letter relative to `A` (65) or `a` (97).
`let k = ((shift % 26) + 26) % 26` and for letters: `Character(UnicodeScalar((Int(ascii - base) + k) % 26 + Int(base))!)`.
jsBridge: JS does `String.fromCharCode(((c - 65 + k) % 26 + 26) % 26 + 65)`. Swift works on `Character.asciiValue` (`UInt8?`) and `UnicodeScalar`. The `%` remainder can be negative in both languages, so the double-mod trick carries over.
